notes.inflation: Two inflation measures are shown. The Czech Statistical Office's national CPI is the headline figure and the one the Czech National Bank targets at 2%; it includes owner-occupied housing costs, which the EU-harmonised HICP leaves out, so the two can differ by a few tenths. The HICP is shown for comparison with other EU countries. The interest rate is the CNB's two-week repo rate, shown from January 1998, when the CNB adopted inflation targeting.
notes.labour: Unemployment is Eurostat's monthly, seasonally adjusted rate (ILO definition, ages 15 to 74). Czech news often quotes the Labour Office's registered unemployment share instead, a different and higher measure. Employment and participation rates are the OECD's quarterly figures for ages 15 to 64.
notes.trade: Goods trade is Eurostat's monthly total with the rest of the world, converted from euros to koruna at each month's ECB reference rate, so figures differ slightly from the Czech Statistical Office's own, which follow the change of ownership of goods. All three series end at the latest month for which both exports and imports are published.
notes.public: Debt and the budget balance are Eurostat's excessive deficit procedure figures for general government, calendar years.
notes.markets: The 10-year yield is the ECB's monthly long-term interest rate for convergence purposes for Czechia. The exchange rates are World Bank annual averages of the official koruna rate, so they move once a year; there is no free daily or monthly series for the koruna on the Federal Reserve's H.10 list.
